inline_comments.comment:
Setting `include` explicitly overrides the plugin default entirely — it is not additive. The comment only explains the new workspace path entry, leaving the `'**/**.tsx'` line unexplained. A user who reads the prose ('add your workspace package source files to the `include` option') and manually extends their config with only their workspace path will silently drop `'**/**.tsx'`, causing all of their own project's components to lose prop documentation. Add a clarifying comment on that line, e.g.:
```ts
// Keep the default so local project .tsx files are still included
'**/**.tsx',
// Add your workspace package source files so they're included in the TS program
'../../packages/ui/src/**/*.tsx',
```
Or add a prose note: 'Note: setting `include` overrides the default — be sure to keep `**/**.tsx` so your own project's components are still covered.'

The explanation mentions 'the underlying Vite plugin' but this section is rendered for all React projects, including webpack-based ones (`@storybook/react-webpack5`). Webpack uses `react-docgen-typescript-loader`, which has different `include` semantics. A webpack user who lands on this troubleshooting entry will try the same fix to no effect. Consider adding a qualifier such as 'This applies to Vite-based React frameworks (e.g., `@storybook/react-vite`, `@storybook/nextjs-vite`)' at the start of the explanation, or wrapping the entire entry in a Vite-specific conditional if the docs system supports it.

The placeholder comment in the CSF Next block (line 21) is inconsistent with the CSF 3 block (line 2) in two ways: punctuation (`e.g.` vs `e.g.,`) and listed frameworks (`react-vite, nextjs, vue3-vite, etc.` vs `react-vite, nextjs, nextjs-vite`). Align the two comments — the CSF Next block should match the CSF 3 style or vice versa.
